sections.title: My toys

q.prompt: Which word means “a toy that flies in the wind”?
q.reason: “kite” means a toy that flies in the wind.

options.fb: “ball” means a round toy you kick or throw.
“doll” means a toy that looks like a person.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 2. In this lesson: My toys.
Name toys and say what is yours with ‘my / your / his / her’.
Here are some new words. Kite. A toy that flies in the wind. Doll.
A toy that looks like a person. Ball. A round toy you kick or throw.
Listen and say them. kite
doll
ball.
And some more words. Train. A toy with carriages on a track. Robot.
A machine toy that can move. Puzzle. A game where you put pieces together.
Listen and say them. train
robot
puzzle.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a toy that flies in the wind?
Now some grammar: my and your and his and her.
These words say who something belongs to. For example: This is my kite.
For example: That is her doll.
Now listen, and read along. The toy box. Leo and his sister Noor open the toy box.
‘Here is my robot!’ says Leo. His robot can walk and talk.
‘Here is my puzzle!’ says Noor. Her puzzle has got a hundred pieces.
‘Where is our ball?’ asks Leo. It is under the box!
They play with the ball in the garden.
Another question. The video will stop. Who is Leo's sister?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like kite, doll, ball.
You practised my and your and his and her. And you read The toy box.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 2. In this lesson: Let's play a game!
Follow and give simple instructions.
Here are some new words. Jump. Push off the ground with your legs. Run.
Move very fast on your legs. Throw. Send something through the air with your hand.
Listen and say them. jump
run
throw.
And some more words. Catch. Take something that is flying in the air. Turn.
It is your time to play. Win. Be the best in a game. Listen and say them. catch
turn
win.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: push off the ground with your legs?
Now some grammar: Instructions. Instructions start with a doing word (verb).
We use ‘Let's’ to make a suggestion. For example: Throw the ball.
For example: Let's play!
Now listen, and read along. How to play ‘Animal Statues’.
You need: music and three or more friends. 1. Play some music. 2.
Dance like an animal – a monkey, a frog or a bird! 3. When the music stops, stop!
Be a statue. 4. Don't move! If you move, you are out. 5.
The last player in the game is the winner.
Another question. The video will stop. What do you need?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like jump, run, throw.
You practised instructions. And you read How to play ‘Animal Statues’.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

req.ctx:
How to play ‘Animal Statues’
You need: music and three or more friends.
1. Play some music.
2. Dance like an animal – a monkey, a frog or a bird!
3. When the music stops, stop! Be a statue.
4. Don't move! If you move, you are out.
5. The last player in the game is the winner.
